arxiv-2101-08808.title: Refining Network Alignment to Improve Matched Neighborhood Consistency
arxiv-2101-08808.creator: Mark Heimann, Xiyuan Chen, Fatemeh Vahedian, Danai Koutra
arxiv-2101-08808.description: Abstract Network alignment, or the task of finding meaningful node correspondences between nodes in different graphs, is an important graph mining task with many scientific and industrial applications. An important principle for network alignment is matched neighborhood consistency (MNC): nodes that are close in one graph should be matched to nodes that are close in the other graph.

arxiv-2108-10170.title: Dual variational formulations for a large class of non-convex models in the calculus of variations
arxiv-2108-10170.creator: Fabio Silva Botelho
arxiv-2108-10170.description: Abstract This article develops dual variational formulations for a large class of models in variational optimization. The results are established through basic tools of functional analysis, convex analysis and duality theory. The main duality principle is developed as an application to a Ginzburg-Landau type system in superconductivity in the absence of a magnetic field.

arxiv-2310-11895.title: Flexible Computation Offloading at the Edge for Autonomous Drones with Uncertain Flight Times
arxiv-2310-11895.creator: Giorgos Polychronis and Spyros Lalis
arxiv-2310-11895.description: Abstract An ever increasing number of applications can employ aerial unmanned vehicles, or so-called drones, to perform different sensing and possibly also actuation tasks from the air. In some cases, the data that is captured at a given point has to be processed before moving to the next one.

arxiv-2410-11889.title: Preservation of dissipativity in dimensionality reduction
arxiv-2410-11889.creator: Sergey V. Stasenko, Alexander N. Kirdin
arxiv-2410-11889.description: Abstract Systems with predetermined Lyapunov functions play an important role in many areas of applied mathematics, physics and engineering: dynamic optimization methods (objective functions and their modifications), machine learning (loss functions), thermodynamics and kinetics (free energy and other thermodynamic potentials), adaptive control (various objective functions, stabilization quality criteria and other Lyapunov functions).

arxiv-2502-17681.title: Properties of ‘Lite’ Intermediate-Mass Black Hole Candidates in LIGO-Virgo’s Third Observing Run
arxiv-2502-17681.creator: Krystal Ruiz-Rocha, Anjali B. Yelikar, Jacob Lange, William Gabella, Robert A. Weller, Richard O’Shaughnessy, Kelly Holley-Bockelmann, Karan Jani
arxiv-2502-17681.description: Abstract Over a hundred gravitational-wave (GW) detections and candidates have been reported from the first three observing runs of the Advanced LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) detectors. Among these, the most intriguing events are binary black hole mergers that result in a ‘lite’ intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) of ∼ 10 2 ​ M ⊙ {\sim}10^{2}~\mathrm{M}_{\odot} , such as GW170502 and GW190521.

pmc-10603195.title: Decoding the host–pathogen interspecies molecular crosstalk during oral candidiasis in humans: an in silico analysis
pmc-10603195.creator: Ali Rejwan Kabir, Anis Ahmad Chaudhary, Malak O. Aladwani, Soumita Podder
pmc-10603195.description: Introduction: The objective of this study is to investigate the interaction between Candida albicans and human proteins during oral candidiasis, with the aim of identifying pathways through which the pathogen subverts host cells. Methods: A comprehensive list of interactions between human proteins and C. albicans was obtained from the Human Protein Interaction Database using specific screening criteria.

pmc-10643667.title: Diet-derived male sex pheromone compounds affect female choice in a noctuid moth
pmc-10643667.creator: Naomi L. Zweerus, Michiel van Wijk, Coby Schal, Astrid T. Groot
pmc-10643667.description: Sexual signals often function in species recognition and may also guide mate choice within a species. In noctuid moths, both males and females may exercise mate choice. Females of the tobacco budworm Chloridea virescens prefer to mate with larger males, but the signal(s) underlying female choice remain unknown. Male hairpencil volatiles are emitted during close range courtship displays.

pmc-10707673.title: Neuroadaptive Biochemical Mechanisms of Remote Ischemic Conditioning
pmc-10707673.creator: Ksenia Baranova, Natalia Nalivaeva, Elena Rybnikova
pmc-10707673.description: This review summarizes the currently known biochemical neuroadaptive mechanisms of remote ischemic conditioning. In particular, it focuses on the significance of the pro-adaptive effects of remote ischemic conditioning which allow for the prevention of the neurological and cognitive impairments associated with hippocampal dysregulation after brain damage.

pmc-11326570.title: A guide for the generation of repositories of clinical samples for research on Chagas disease
pmc-11326570.creator: Nieves Martínez-Peinado, Juan Carlos Gabaldón-Figueira, Roberto Rodrigues Ferreira, María Carmen Thomas, Manuel Carlos López, Tania Cremonini Araújo-Jorge, Belkisyolé Alarcón de Noya, Soledad Berón, Janine Ramsey, Irene Losada Galván, Alejandro Gabriel Schijman, Adriana González Martínez, Andrés Mar
pmc-11326570.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Chagas disease, caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, affects over 6 million people, mainly in Latin America. Two different clinical phases, acute and chronic, are recognised. Currently, 2 anti-parasitic drugs are available to treat the disease (nifurtimox and benznidazole), but diagnostic methods require of a relatively complex infrastructure and trained personnel, limiting its widespread use in endemic areas, and the access of patients to treatment.

pmc-11380057.title: AI-Driven Diagnostic Assistance in Medical Inquiry: Reinforcement Learning Algorithm Development and Validation
pmc-11380057.creator: Xuan Zou, Weijie He, Yu Huang, Yi Ouyang, Zhen Zhang, Yu Wu, Yongsheng Wu, Lili Feng, Sheng Wu, Mengqi Yang, Xuyan Chen, Yefeng Zheng, Rui Jiang, Ting Chen, Simone Ma, Hyeonhoon Lee, Taavi Tillmann
pmc-11380057.description: BackgroundFor medical diagnosis, clinicians typically begin with a patient’s chief concerns, followed by questions about symptoms and medical history, physical examinations, and requests for necessary auxiliary examinations to gather comprehensive medical information. This complex medical investigation process has yet to be modeled by existing artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies.

pmc-11387423.title: Abnormal left atrial strain and left atrial stiffness index are associated with adverse outcomes in children with cardiomyopathies: a pilot study
pmc-11387423.creator: Katarzyna Łuczak-Woźniak, Cezary Niszczota, Klaudia Obsznajczyk, Bożena Werner
pmc-11387423.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Conventional diastolic dysfunction parameters seem to be imperfect when applied to the pediatric cardiomyopathy population. The aim of this pilot study was to search for novel echocardiographic parameters associated with adverse outcomes in children with the most common cardiomyopathies. Fifty-six patients with pediatric cardiomyopathies (28 with dilated, 21 with hypertrophic, 7 with left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy) and 28 healthy subjects were included in the study.

pmc-11489723.title: The socioeconomic and environmental niche of protected areas reveals global conservation gaps and opportunities
pmc-11489723.creator: David Mouillot, Laure Velez, Camille Albouy, Nicolas Casajus, Joachim Claudet, Vincent Delbar, Rodolphe Devillers, Tom B. Letessier, Nicolas Loiseau, Stéphanie Manel, Laura Mannocci, Jessica Meeuwig, Nicolas Mouquet, Ana Nuno, Louise O’Connor, Valeriano Parravicini, Julien Renaud, Raphael Seguin, Ma
pmc-11489723.description: The global network of protected areas has rapidly expanded in the past decade and is expected to cover at least 30% of land and sea by 2030 to halt biodiversity erosion. Yet, the distribution of protected areas is highly heterogeneous on Earth and the social-environmental preconditions enabling or hindering protected area establishment remain poorly understood.

pmc-11629482.title: Surgery for bronchiectasis in children living with HIV: A case series from a low- to middle-income country
pmc-11629482.creator: H Peens-Hough, P Goussard, D Rhode, L van Wyk, J Janson
pmc-11629482.description: Background Bronchiectasis (BE) in children living with HIV (CLWH) remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, especially in tuberculosis (TB)-endemic low- and middle-income countries. Treatment modalities for BE in CLWH currently focus mainly on prevention of infections and management of symptoms, while surgical management is indicated for a select group.

pmc-12391690.title: Genomic characterization and comparative analysis of antibiotic resistance and virulence in Bangladeshi and global Klebsiella pneumoniae ST48 strains
pmc-12391690.creator: Sudipta Chowdhury Chaity, Md Arman Hosen, Sabita Rezwana Rahman, Md Abu Sayem Khan
pmc-12391690.description: Highlights•Klebsiella pneumoniae S3C was multidrug-resistant, a moderate biofilm former, and belonged to the ST48 clonal type.•Genomic analysis of Bangladeshi populations of ST48 revealed multidrug resistance and a rich virulome.•blaCTX-M-15 was detected in 96.08% of the genomes of ST48 populations in Bangladesh.•Pan-genome analysis of global K. pneumoniae ST48 populations revealed high genomic plasticity and an open pan-genome.

pmc-12538950.description: This study explores patient flow logistics (PFL) from strategic and tactical viewpoints, introducing a decision-making framework to systematically categorize key challenges. pmc-12587509.title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolism after knee arthroscopy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12587509.creator: Wei Zheng, Xing Jin, Mingming Yao, Zhiting Dong, Wei He
pmc-12587509.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundOver the past few years, a growing number of knee arthroscopy (KA) procedures have been associated with an escalating incidence of postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE), posing a significant threat to patient well-being.

pmc-12622578.title: Effect of early shoulder functional exercise timing on drainage duration and subcutaneous seroma formation in overweight women undergoing modified radical mastectomy for breast cancer
pmc-12622578.creator: Zengyan Wang, Qinghai Lin, Xiong Wu
pmc-12622578.description: This retrospective study investigates the impact of early postoperative shoulder functional exercise timing on drainage duration and subcutaneous seroma formation in overweight women undergoing modified radical mastectomy (MRM) for breast cancer. A total of 194 overweight breast cancer patients (BMI > 24) who underwent MRM between January 2023 and December 2024 were included.

pmc-13202021.title: Treatment Outcomes and Prognostic Factors of Metastasis-Directed Radiation Therapy for Oligometastatic Endometrial Cancer
pmc-13202021.creator: Won Hee Lee, Yong Bae Kim
pmc-13202021.description: PurposeTo evaluate outcomes and prognostic factors associated with metastasis-directed radiation therapy (MDRT) for oligometastatic endometrial cancer.Methods and MaterialsWe retrospectively analyzed 101 patients (203 lesions) with ≤5 metastatic lesions treated with MDRT between 2015 and 2025. Oligometastatic states were classified according to the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology–European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer framework.

pmc-13232484.title: AURKA inhibitor VIC-1911 induces mitotic defects and functional BRCAness, sensitizing prostate cancer to PARP inhibition
pmc-13232484.creator: Galina Gritsina, Sandip Kumar Rath, Hongshun Shi, Qi Chu, Wanqing Xie, Que Thanh Thanh Nguyen, Sambhavi Senthil, Thomas J Myers, Mehmet A Bilen, Sarah E Fenton, Maha Hussain, David S Yu, Jonathan C Zhao, Jindan Yu
pmc-13232484.description: VIC-1911 (formerly TAS-119) is a next-generation, ATP-competitive aurora kinase A (AURKA) inhibitor with a favorable biosafety profile. However, it has not been evaluated in prostate cancer (PCa), wherein AURKA is highly expressed in advanced stages and represents a critical therapeutic target. Here, we demonstrate that VIC-1911 potently inhibits AURKA activity with high selectivity over AURKB/C across diverse PCa cell lines.

pmc-13365951.title: IFPHPOS0057 The Relationship Between Income-Generating Activities of Women, Dietary Behaviours and Feeding Practices of Infants and Young Children in Urban Ghana
pmc-13365951.creator: Jedidah Mould, Emily Rousham, Katherine Gough, James Esson
pmc-13365951.description: BackgroundMalnutrition remains a major public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, including Ghana, particularly among children aged 6–23 months, a critical window for growth and development. Maternal income-generating activities (IGAs) may influence infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices through improved income but also reduced caregiving time.
